subject: Risk & Compliance
title: The German Two-Tier Board
description: A quick win: understand The German Two-Tier Board.

hook.text: German companies have two boards: one manages, the other supervises. Workers sit on the supervisory board.

buildup.text: The management board runs the company. The supervisory board — including employee representatives — oversees it.

discovery.text: Codetermination gives workers up to half the seats on supervisory boards of large German companies.

twist.text: Worker representation brings a long-term perspective but can slow down decisions that affect jobs.

climax.text: Germany's model shows governance isn't just for shareholders. Workers have a legitimate voice too.

punchline.text: Workers on the board. Long-term thinking. A different model.

quiz.question: What is codetermination in German governance?
options: Workers get seats on the supervisory board
Two CEOs share all decisions equally
